# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-ref-low

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

`coop --git` (two agents with messaging and a shared git remote) with the frozen reference settings (`gemini-3.8-flash` on Vertex AI, 500 steps, compaction at 128K tokens, step counter, `$40` per-agent cost cap) at `low` thinking instead of the default `medium`, on the 50-pair `flash` subset. It is the `low` row of the agreed thinking sweep and pairs with the [`solo` reference run at `low`](../solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-ref-low/summary.md).

## Observations

- 34/50 (68%) at `low` vs. 35/50 at `medium` with the same settings (1 pair only at `low`, 2 only at `medium`): unlike `solo`, `coop --git` does about as well at `low` as at `medium` at 128K.
- Against `solo` at `low` with the same settings (30/50): 5 pairs passed only here and 1 only in `solo`. With the reference settings the two settings trade places by thinking level (`coop --git` ahead at `low`, `solo` ahead at `medium`, 37 vs. 35), and every gap is within run-to-run variation.
- The two earlier `coop --git` `low` runs at 64K both scored 30/50; this run gained 5 and 6 pairs against them while losing 1 and 2. That points the same way as 128K's effect on `solo` at `medium`, though it is not conclusive on its own.
- Both `pallets_click_task/2068` pairs where agents had previously worked around a shared line ((6,7) and (7,10)) passed: on (6,7) one agent changed the shared `Editor(...)` call for both features.
- All 50 pairs merged cleanly (45 clean, 5 identical branches), median 25 messages per pair, median 79 steps per agent. One agent on `pallets_click_task/2068` (5,7) stopped at step 13 with a harness error ("list index out of range"), and that pair failed. Cost `$48.96`, 170 minutes, 2 retries, no false "partner stopped" notices.
